subject: Pilot economics: hybrid savings framework & quantization guidance
messages:
From: Zoe Park <zoe.park@ledgerai.com>
To: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@ledgerai.com
Date: Tue, 01 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood pilot — clarifying credits vs unit pricing for caching/quant work

Hi Aditya,

Thanks again for yesterday's demo. LedgerAI is excited about the latency profile and your cache/batching approach — the savings look promising. Before procurement can move forward we need clarity on two items for the proposed 3-month pilot:

1) How the pilot credits would reconcile with committed units if we convert to a paid plan mid-pilot (credits applied vs per-token billing).
2) Whether Redwood will support the recommended int8 quant build for our model family (open-source variant) and whether that qualifies for additional "quantization credits" in your commercial model.

Can you share a short one-page summary and a sample credit schedule we can circulate internally?

- Zoe
Procurement Lead, LedgerAI

From: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Zoe Park <zoe.park@ledgerai.com>, procurement@ledgerai.com
Cc: monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Jun 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood pilot — clarifying credits vs unit pricing for caching/quant work

Zoe — great question, thanks. Short answers up top, details below and attached: pilot-econ-summary-v1.pdf + sample-credit-schedule.xlsx.

TL;DR
- Pilot credits are fully reconcilable: any unused pilot credits convert to a one-time credit on the first invoice if you commit to a 12-month reserved band within 30 days of pilot end.
- If you convert to a committed plan mid-pilot we pro-rate consumed units against the commitment; remaining pilot credits are applied as offset.
- Redwood will support the int8 quantization we recommended; models validated on our int8 flow receive a 15% per-token "quant credit" applied to generated tokens for 6 months post-rollout.

Notes (economics)
- Hybrid savings framework proposal: combine a modest reserved-commitment band (to guarantee throughput and provide runway) + dynamic pilot credits that reward observed cache hit-rate and KV-prefix reuse.
- Example: For a pilot sized at 500k generated tokens/day with an observed 35% prefix/KV cache hit rate and our recommended batching (avg batch size 8), modeled delivered unit cost drops ~48% vs on-demand. If you move to a 6-month reserved band at 30% commit, list per-token price reduces further; sample sheet outlines bands.

Quantization
- We will run your open model through our int8 pipeline during the pilot. If accuracy regressions are within the agreed guardrails (<1.5% degrade on your eval set), LedgerAI qualifies for the 15% quant credit; else we offer a remediation run and additional tuning time at no charge.

Attached: pilot-econ-summary-v1.pdf (one-pager), sample-credit-schedule.xlsx, redwood-quant-recommendation-notes.txt

Next step: Monica will propose a short mutual action plan and a procurement-friendly credit schedule.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Zoe Park <zoe.park@ledgerai.com>, procurement@ledgerai.com
Cc: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 02 Jun 2027 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood pilot — clarifying credits vs unit pricing for caching/quant work

Hi Zoe — looping in a concise MAP below. Happy to jump on a 30m call to walk procurement through the schedule later this week.

Mutual Action Plan (draft)
- Week 0 (kickoff): Exchange access and I/O specs; Redwood runs baseline perf/throughput capture (no charge).
- Week 1–2: Quantization pass & validation on Redwood infra; measure accuracy, latency, and KV cache behavior.
- Week 3–8: Pilot (3 calendar months) with 250k–500k gen tokens/day baseline. Redwood provides pilot credits upfront: 1M generated-token credits + 300k KV-cache-credits for served cached prefixes.
- Pilot reconciliation: At pilot end, LedgerAI chooses 1) self-serve on-demand, 2) convert to reserved band (1/3/6/12 mo) — unused credits applied to first invoice or to top-up for reserved band conversion.

Commercial ask and concessions
- We can offer an initial 20% off list per-token price for first 6 months if you commit to a minimum 3-month reserved band after pilot.
- If LedgerAI commits to a 12-month reserved band within 30 days of pilot close, we will extend the quant credit to 9 months and include 1x free model tuning sprint.

Please confirm a good time for a Friday 30m to run procurement through the schedule.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Solutions Director | Redwood Inference

From: Zoe Park <zoe.park@ledgerai.com>
To: monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@ledgerai.com
Date: Thu, 03 Jun 2027 10:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood pilot — clarifying credits vs unit pricing for caching/quant work

Monica — thanks, this is helpful. A couple of clarifying questions from procurement:
1) How exactly are the KV-cache-credits measured and applied? We want a simple reconciliation line on the invoice.
2) Can you confirm whether the 20% concession stacks with the 15% quant credit (i.e., applied sequentially or concurrently)?

Also procurement asks for a short redline-friendly MSA excerpt for pilot terms (limit liability, data handling, pilot credit mechanics). Can you attach?

- Zoe

From: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Zoe Park <zoe.park@ledgerai.com>, procurement@ledgerai.com
Cc: monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 05 Jun 2027 16:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood pilot — clarifying credits vs unit pricing for caching/quant work

Zoe — quick answers inline + attached a short pilot MSA excerpt for procurement to redline (pilot-msa-excerpt.pdf).

1) KV-cache-credits: We instrument cache hits at request-level. Each time a token sequence is served from the KV/prefix cache we increment the cache-hit token counter. At invoicing we report: generated-tokens, cached-token-saves, and net billed tokens = generated - cached-token-saves. The invoice will show a single reconciliation line: "Pilot credit applied (cached token savings)" with the number of tokens and credit amount. We will also provide a CSV export of the cache-hit events for audit.

2) Discount stacking: the 20% concession is applied to the base per-token list first, then the quant credit (15%) is applied to the resulting per-token cost — effectively sequential stacking. We've modeled both stacking and non-stacking in the attached sample-credit-schedule.xlsx; you can toggle assumptions on tab 'stacking-models'.

Action items
- Zoe / procurement: confirm whether LedgerAI wants the invoice to break out cache-saved tokens line-by-line or just as the single reconciliation line.
- LedgerAI: confirm Friday or Monday for a 30m procurement walkthrough.

Attachments: pilot-msa-excerpt.pdf (pilot terms excerpt), sample-credit-schedule.xlsx (stacking scenarios)

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
